genes/MYCTU/groEL2/groEL2-ai-review.yaml.description: GroEL2 (Cpn60.2) is the essential housekeeping chaperonin of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It supports ATP-dependent protein folding with GroES, while purified lower oligomers can also suppress aggregation and partially refold substrates independently of ATP or GroES. Its assembly and ATPase activity depend strongly on solution conditions. Extracellular and surface-associated GroEL2 participates in macrophage adhesion, and a proteolytically cleaved form reaches host mitochondria and modulates apoptotic responses.

genes/ECOLI/groS/groS-ai-review.yaml.description: GroS, also called GroES or Cpn10, is the small heptameric co-chaperonin lid of the essential E. coli GroEL-GroES chaperonin. Each GroES ring binds the apical surface of a GroEL heptamer and caps the cis GroEL chamber, allowing ATP-driven encapsulation of non-native proteins in a protected hydrophilic cage that promotes folding and prevents aggregation. GroES cycles on and off GroEL during assisted protein folding in the bacterial cytosol and is also required as a host chaperonin factor for assembly of several bacteriophages.

core_functions.description: GroES directly binds the GroEL protein-folding chaperone as a heptameric co-chaperonin and contributes to ATP-dependent protein folding by the GroEL-GroES chamber. GroES capping reorients the GroEL apical domains, buries hydrophobic peptide-binding residues, and stabilizes the hydrophilic folding chamber in which non-native polypeptides are released and assisted toward their native fold.
